intended_object: A (locally v-small) category structure on a type of objects C: a type of morphisms Hom(X, Y) for each pair of objects, with identities and composition, satisfying the left and right unit laws and associativity. This comes from the docstring, the Stacks tag 0014 and the Wikidata item Q719395.
explanation:
This is Mathlib's own basic definition of a category, so there is no other Mathlib counterpart to cite. It extends `CategoryStruct`, which supplies the hom-types `X ⟶ Y : Type v`, the identities `𝟙 X` and the composition `≫`. On top of that it requires the three standard axioms: `𝟙 X ≫ f = f`, `f ≫ 𝟙 Y = f`, and `(f ≫ g) ≫ h = f ≫ g ≫ h`.

The definition puts no restriction on the universe levels of objects and morphisms. Small, large and locally small categories are all special cases of it. This is the usual type-theoretic way to write the textbook definition of a category, with hom-sets given as types, and it is fully general.
